tldr: MART (MLLM As ReTriever) fine-tunes an MLLM retriever using interactive preference learning so it can identify the most task-effective trajectories for embodied agents in unseen environments, combined with a Trajectory Abstraction mechanism to condense trajectories while preserving key milestones.
contributions: First approach integrating interactive learning with a retriever, using interactive feedback to fine-tune an MLLM retriever for evaluating trajectory effectiveness
Trajectory Abstraction mechanism that uses MLLM summarization to condense trajectories, reducing average input from 11.51 steps to 3.13 milestones while retaining essential information
Empirical validation across AI2-THOR and LEGENT environments showing MART surpasses baselines by over 10%
methods: For each training task, K expert trajectories are sampled from memory and provided as prompts to an MLLM agent (LLaVA-7B), which executes the task to obtain success rates. These rates form preference pairs (higher-success vs. lower-success trajectories) used to fine-tune the MLLM retriever with a Bradley-Terry loss, adding a one-layer MLP score head to the hidden states. A separate MLLM (GPT-4o) performs Trajectory Abstraction by identifying milestone observations that are useful for the current task, compressing trajectories while preserving key information. During inference, the fine-tuned retriever scores candidate trajectories and selects the highest-scoring one as the reference for the embodied agent.
results: MART achieves significantly higher task success rates than baselines across AI2-THOR and LEGENT environments. MART consistently surpasses baseline methods by over 10% across different environments. Trajectory Abstraction reduces average input trajectory length from 11.51 steps to 3.13 milestones while preserving essential information.
limitations: Memory pool size is relatively small: 40 training trajectories and 32 test trajectories in LEGENT, and 170/118 trajectories in AI2-THOR
Trajectory Abstraction relies on an external MLLM (GPT-4o), introducing additional dependency and potential cost
The paper does not demonstrate results at significantly larger scale beyond the tested environments
